writtenTo: The seven churches in Asia Minor (and all believers)
importantNotes: Revelation is the only book that promises a blessing to those who read it (1:3).
The book uses over 500 allusions to the Old Testament — it is deeply rooted in Scripture.
'Behold, I am making all things new' (21:5) — God's final word is restoration, not destruction.
The letters to the seven churches (chs. 2-3) apply to all churches in every age.
The book was written during persecution — its message is comfort and hope, not fear.

chapters.1: The revelation of Jesus Christ; a vision of the glorified Son of Man among the seven churches.
chapters.2: Letters to the churches at Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira.
chapters.3: Letters to the churches at Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea — 'I stand at the door and knock.'
chapters.4: A vision of God's throne in heaven — the twenty-four elders and four living creatures worship.
chapters.5: The Lamb alone is worthy to open the sealed scroll — worship from all creation.
chapters.6: The first six seals are opened — conquest, war, famine, death, martyrs, cosmic upheaval.
chapters.7: The 144,000 are sealed; a great multitude from every nation worships before the throne.
chapters.8: The seventh seal; the first four trumpet judgments — hail, blood, fire, and darkness.
chapters.9: The fifth and sixth trumpet judgments — demonic locusts and a deadly army.
chapters.10: The mighty angel with the little scroll; John eats the scroll — sweet then bitter.
chapters.11: The two witnesses prophesy, are killed, and are resurrected; the seventh trumpet sounds.
chapters.12: The woman, the child, and the dragon; war in heaven; Satan cast down to earth.
chapters.13: The beast from the sea and the beast from the earth; the mark of the beast — 666.
chapters.14: The Lamb on Mount Zion; the three angels' messages; the harvest of the earth.
chapters.15: The seven angels with the seven last plagues; the song of Moses and the Lamb.
chapters.16: The seven bowls of God's wrath poured out on the earth; Armageddon.
chapters.17: The great prostitute Babylon riding the scarlet beast — mystery Babylon explained.
chapters.18: The fall of Babylon — 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!' — merchants mourn.
chapters.19: The heavenly hallelujah; the marriage supper of the Lamb; Christ returns as King of Kings.
chapters.20: Satan bound for 1,000 years; the millennium; the great white throne judgment.
chapters.21: The new heaven and new earth; the New Jerusalem descends; God dwells with His people — no more tears.
chapters.22: The river of life; the tree of life; Jesus is coming soon — 'Come, Lord Jesus!'
